findings.problem: status is a raw String, allowing illegal values like "sent", "", "SENT", or any future value not in the domain language. Holzman requires replacing status strings with enums.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid status strings slip through at runtime; callers cannot exhaustively match on states; the compiler cannot enforce workflow invariants.
findings.fix: Replace `pub status: String` with an enum, e.g. `enum LedgerStatus { Draft, Sent }`, and construct only valid variants.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool is a primitive lifecycle flag. Holzman requires replacing bool lifecycle flags with enums or typestates. These flags are also redundant with `status` and `is_sent`, creating contradictory state.
findings.failure_mode: The struct can hold contradictory combinations such as status="sent" with is_sent=false, or is_validated=true with status="draft". Illegal states are representable.
findings.fix: Eliminate `is_validated` and `is_sent` entirely. Fold the validation lifecycle into the domain enum or use a proper typestate pattern with distinct types per workflow stage.

findings.problem: is_sent: bool is a primitive lifecycle flag, redundant with status="sent". Holzman requires replacing bool lifecycle flags with enums or typestates.
findings.failure_mode: The struct can represent impossible states (e.g. is_sent=true but status="draft"). No compile-time enforcement of the sent lifecycle invariant.
findings.fix: Fold the sent state into the domain enum or use a typestate (e.g. `LedgerSent` vs `LedgerDraft`). Remove `is_sent` as a redundant field.

findings.problem: LedgerWorkflow has no constructor and all fields are pub. Any combination of status/bools is constructable, including logically impossible ones (e.g. is_sent=true, is_validated=false, status="draft").
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code can read a struct in an inconsistent state, causing silent logic errors, incorrect sent detection, or failed assertions at runtime instead of compile-time enforcement.
findings.fix: Make all fields private, provide a fallible constructor or builder, and use enums/typestates so illegal combinations are unrepresentable at compile time.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes a mutable struct and mutates it in place (item.status = ..., item.is_sent = ...). This is imperative mutation, not a pure functional core transition. The function has no validation — it blindly sets fields.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can invoke mark_sent regardless of the ledger's current state (e.g. from "draft" or already "sent"), with no state-transition guard. No purity, no invariants checked.
findings.fix: Use a pure function that takes `LedgerDraft` (or equivalent pre-sent typestate) and returns `LedgerSent`. The type system enforces the valid transition. Return `Result<LedgerSent, TransitionError>` if runtime checks are needed.

findings.problem: id is a raw String. Holzman requires replacing primitive domain values with newtypes when they carry domain rules.
findings.failure_mode: Ledger IDs cannot carry domain invariants (length, format, uniqueness) at the type level. Any string is accepted.
findings.fix: Introduce a `LedgerId` newtype with a fallible constructor that validates domain rules. Use `LedgerId` instead of `String`.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> stores a raw timestamp. If is_sent were removed in favor of a typestate, the timestamp should live only in the sent typestate, not alongside a redundant bool flag.
findings.failure_mode: Timestamp is present or absent independently of the actual sent state, creating another inconsistency vector.
findings.fix: Move the timestamp into the typestate that represents the sent lifecycle stage, or use a dedicated `SentTimestamp` newtype with validation (non-zero, monotonic).

findings.problem: item.status = "sent".to_string() allocates a new String on every call. In a pure core pattern, the status should be an enum variant (zero-cost) rather than an allocated string.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation per transition. Enum variants are zero-cost and avoid the allocation entirely.
findings.fix: Replace String status with an enum. Enum variants are stack-allocated and zero-cost.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for the stated or implied performance characteristics
no profiler output (flamegraph/callgrind) for the transition path
no allocation profiling (e.g. heaptrack/valgrind --leak-check or Rust alloc counters)
no second-ring validation evidence (property tests or fuzz tests for state transitions)
no command/CLI interface to exercise the ledger workflow end-to-end
residual_risk: The struct encodes illegal states by construction. The mark_sent function performs unguarded mutation with no typestate or enum discipline. Without type-level enforcement, any caller can place a LedgerWorkflow into an inconsistent state at runtime. Static review only; no commands run.
